reply_text:
Found **one merge-blocking bug** in `share-editing` (`1dc003f`):

**[P1] View-only shares can edit unlocked documents — `src/guard.js:12`**

```js
return share.mask & WRITE === WRITE && !share.locked;
```

JavaScript evaluates `===` before `&`, so this effectively checks the **READ bit**, not WRITE. Confirmed:
- `canEdit({ mask: READ, locked: false })` → `true`: a viewer can edit.
- `canEdit({ mask: WRITE, locked: false })` → `0`: a write-only share cannot edit.

Use `hasRight(share.mask, WRITE) && !share.locked`, consistent with `canComment`. Add regression tests for those two cases.

All six existing tests pass, but they miss this because the tested editor has both READ and WRITE. I also checked toggling across all rights masks and ownership transfer’s documented rights behavior; no additional issues found.

No code changed. **I’d fix the permission check before merging.**

first_step_runs.command: cd /root/workspace/repo && cat README.md package.json CHANGELOG.md && git diff main...share-editing && find src test -type f -maxdepth 3 -print

# notebin

Sharing permissions for notebin documents.

Each share stores its rights as a bit mask (src/rights.js): READ 1, COMMENT 2, WRITE 4, ADMIN 8. A viewer link has READ only. An editor has READ, COMMENT and WRITE. The owner has all four.

Check a right with hasRight(mask, right).
